text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: inference-rt-prod pod node-7 reported repeated GPU allocation failures (cudaMalloc) leading to 503s for requests routed to model-x-1. Customer impact: intermittent request failures and elevated latency. On-call: samir.

samir: grabbing this. is traffic still flowing to that pool?

liz: still routing, but 3/8 workers on node-7 are unhealthy. Load balancer is retrying and we see spikes in queue time.

andrea: adding initial logs — past 15m nvidia-smi:
```
Fri Mar 10 12:08:15 2026
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id       Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| Fan  Temp  Perf  Pwr:Usage/Cap| Memory-Usage | GPU-Util  Compute M. |
| 0   A100-SXM4       Off       | 0000:18:00.0  Off |                    0 |
| 30%  67C    P2   250W / 400W  | 38948MiB / 40960MiB | 99%      C     
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Process info: model-x-1 worker pids 2145/2150 showing small free chunks but overall freeMem ~2GB. cudaMalloc fails at ~3.5GB request.
```

andrea: also dumping malloc stats from the runtime allocator (jemalloc):
```
arena 0: allocated 3.8G, active 4.0G, metadata 96M
fragmentation ratio ~1.05
peak single allocation failure at 3728MB
```

mike: interesting — fragmentation but no obvious swap. Are we using prefix/KV cache on these workers?

andrea: yes, prefix cache enabled with per-worker reservation 8GB/12GB depending on model. But eviction rate has ticked up.

samir: hypothesis 1: per-request batching + long prefix cache is creating lots of pinned KV memory and small free holes so large allocation fails even with total free. hypothesis 2: allocator fragmentation due to many small allocations from tokenizer + continuous batching.

liz: immediate mitigation options?

samir: 1) reduce max_batch_size on model-x-1 route from 32 -> 16. 2) temporarily disable prefix caching for this model variant. 3) shift some traffic to model-x-2 (lower mem footprint). 4) restart affected workers (last resort).

andrea: I can push a config change to reduce max_batch_size. doing a dry-run on canary first.

mike: I can flip caching off for the pool if needed — that will increase latency but reduce pinned memory.

deploy-bot: deploy request accepted: change model-x-1 max_batch_size -> 16 (canary on node-9), request id deploy-2026-03-10-1532.

samir: canary now. metrics: queue time down slightly.

andrea: tail logs after canary:
```
[12:10:05] worker-2145 batch(28) attempted allocate 3728MB -> cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
[12:10:17] worker-3124 (canary) batch(16) allocate 1800MB -> success
[12:10:19] LB rebalanced 12% traffic to canary
```

mike: after canary success, rolling change to pool: reducing max_batch_size on all nodes in pool to 16. pushing now.

liz: oncall note: customer-facing impact earlier was a 1-3 minute spike per failure, overall error rate for model-x-1 peaked at 4.6% between 12:05–12:12.

samir: live mitigation checklist (doing):
- reduced batch size (in prod) :white_check_mark:
- disabled prefix cache on pool? pending decision
- routing to fallback variant: will shift if errors persist

andrea: I just ran a small memprof script on one worker to dump /proc/<pid>/smaps and GPU allocator fragmentation map. attaching snippet:
```
--- smaps excerpt ---
Size:               204800 kB
Rss:                183420 kB
Pss:                183420 kB
Shared_Clean:           0 kB
KernelPageSize:        64 kB
MMUPageSize:           64 kB
--- holes ---
free ranges: many small holes ~8-64KB, some larger ~1-3MB but none contiguous 3.5GB
```

mike: that smells like fragmentation. jemalloc stats show many small free runs. Another quick mitigation: force periodic compaction / arena purge (jemalloc mallctl purge) between requests — can do but risky for latency.

samir: agree we should avoid that on hot path. Steps: 1) keep reduced batch size for 30m, 2) disable prefix caching on pool if error rate >1% after 30m, 3) collect full jemalloc histograms and GPU vm maps for RCA.

liz: I'll document customer impact and notify support. ETA to update SLA dashboard: 15m.

andrea: starting a background job to capture jemalloc per-arena maps and upload to /artifacts/incidents/1939999999/memdump.tar.gz

mike: a note about cause hypotheses to track in the RCA thread:
- KV/prefix cache reservation holding large contiguous GPU addresses? (less likely, caches often use contiguous allocations)
- allocator fragmentation due to mixed small allocs from tokenizer + medium allocs from KV layers
- CUDA driver-level fragmentation from long-lived allocations and transient big allocations (batch peaks)
- multi-tenant placement on node-7 causing non-uniform memory usage across GPUs

samir: collecting timeline so far: 
- 12:03:12 PM: LB started seeing +5% 5xxs for model-x-1
- 12:04:10 PM: incident-bot created pager
- 12:05:00 PM: metrics show GPU mem ~95% and repeated cudaMalloc failures
- 12:08:30 PM: canary deploy for batch_size=16 started
- 12:10:30 PM: canary success; rolling change to pool started
- 12:14:00 PM: error-rate dropped to ~0.3%

liz: handoff plan: samir, do you want to keep oncall or hand to infra tomorrow morning?

samir: I'll take remainder of shift and feed full RCA notes to infra on Monday. handing to liz for customer comms now.

andrea: follow-ups for RCA: full jemalloc arena dump, GPU address maps (cudaMemGetInfo over time), sample of failing stack traces showing where cudaMalloc requested big contiguous chunk.

mike: runbook additions: consider a quick mitigation toggle for prefix-cache and a per-model max_batch_size safety cap. I'll open a PR.

liz: created support ticket for impacted customers and added note to incident timeline. ticket #INC-2026-1939.

samir: closing live mitigation loop: changes in place reduced failures. we'll keep monitoring for 2 hours. if error rate rises again we escalate to full node drain.

deploy-bot: deploy deploy-2026-03-10-1532 rolled successfully across pool at 12:12:05.

andrea: uploading artifacts: /artifacts/incidents/1939999999/{jemalloc.json, nvidia-smi.txt, smaps.txt}.

samir: thanks everyone. we'll reconvene for an RCA doc tomorrow to finalize root cause and long-term fixes (allocator tuning, cache eviction policy, and safety caps). :memo:

liz: tagging infra and runtime for RCA: @mike @andrea @samir.

incident-bot: incident updated: status -> mitigated.
